MISSION COMPLETE — BESS fault found, reset, and verified; rover returned to dock with arm stowed.

WHAT WAS OBSERVED
1. Initial inspection (telemetry + manifest, before any action): of the five serviced units, only BESS was faulted — breaker tripped, trip_cause OVERTEMP, not energized, resets_since_start 0, BAT-0101 installed in bess_cradle/tray. PDU-1 (habitat life support, crew-critical), PDU-2 (comms, mission-critical), PDU-3 (science), and the ISRU plant were all closed, energized, no trip cause, 0 resets. Manifest showed spare battery module BAT-0102 at depot_spares_stand/slot_0 (not needed). Space context: lunar gravity 1.625 m/s^2; DWE link was up at mission start, Earth set during the run.
2. Pre-intervention evidence at the BESS view pose (33.38, 14.3): front camera saw the BESS panel status lamp RED, independently agreeing with the tripped telemetry.

WHAT WAS DONE
1. BESS HVAC cover: docked at the bess_hvac stand and pressed bess_hvac/cover_button to open the panel cover. Verified press: past button face 6.4 mm, off-axis 0.5 mm, jaws closed empty, retreated, arm folded.
2. BESS breaker reset: docked at bess_panel/press. First press attempt failed at the locate stage — the target I described ("round dark metallic push button") did not match the wrist view (the prominent round object is a white dome). I re-described the target from what the camera actually saw ("single large round white domed push-button cap in a dark grey circular bezel on the flat grey panel face") and the press succeeded.
3. Post-reset verification: re-observed the BESS lamp from its view pose (GREEN), then transited west making a visual lamp check at each remaining unit's surveyed view pose — PDU-3 (23.7, 1.627), PDU-2 (17.2, 1.627), PDU-1 (10.7, 1.627) and ISRU (-30, -5.372). All four showed GREEN lamps.
4. Telemetry re-read four times (t≈781 s, 905 s, and once more at the dock, t≈1000 s): BESS breaker closed, energized true, trip_cause null, resets_since_start 1, BAT-0101 still in bess_cradle/tray. PDU-1/2/3 and ISRU unchanged and nominal throughout. BESS did not re-trip at any point after the reset.
5. Return: navigate_to_pose then dock_to_pose to the rover dock (0,0,0). Verified base_at_commanded_pose (position error 0.026 m, yaw error 0.002 rad). arm_state reads posture stowed, jaw 0.82 rad (open, empty).

VERIFIED EFFECTS
- pressed on bess_hvac/cover_button: holds=true (past_face 0.0064 m, off_axis 0.0005 m, jaws closed empty, retreated 0.71 m).
- pressed on bess_panel/press: holds=true (past_face 0.0064 m, off_axis 0.0005 m, cap_radius 0.032 m, jaw closed empty, retreated 0.71 m).
- base_at_commanded_pose for all navigations and both docks: holds=true; the one press that did not verify (seq 187, holds=false) was the failed locate attempt and was superseded by the successful press at seq 208.
- Restore of BESS confirmed by two independent sources: unit telemetry (breaker closed, energized, no trip cause, resets 1) and the panel lamp seen GREEN by the front camera.
- Rover at dock and arm stowed confirmed by localization and joint encoders.

AUTHORITY
Only the BESS breaker reset was required; it was a panel press, within my own authority. No pick on any energized unit's equipment bay was attempted, so no ground authorization was needed and none is outstanding. No modules were moved; no items were picked or placed.

UNRESOLVED / NOTES
- Root cause of the OVERTEMP trip was not diagnosed beyond what telemetry reports (trip_cause cleared to null after the reset). The BESS radiator/condenser area was not separately inspected; if mission control wants the thermal cause pinned down (radiator fouling, HVAC performance, module BAT-0101 health), that is follow-on work. Spare BAT-0102 remains untouched at depot_spares_stand/slot_0.
- The DWE link is down (Earth below the horizon, reopening in ~1.16e6 s), so this report is store-and-forward and will be delivered at the next pass. No requests to mission control were sent or are pending; no anomalies are unresolved.
